REVIEW: FLAVORS OF GROWTH

 • Norm- and Criterion-Referenced growth

 • Norm-Referenced: Cohort referenced SGPs, Value-Added models

 • Criterion-Referenced: Value tables, baseline referenced/anchored SGPs, student growth
 projections/targets (i.e., growth to standard), catch-up/keep-up/move-up/stay-up.

 • Based upon state preference, policy, and data, different states have created
 different combinations of norm- and criterion-referenced growth metrics.

 • These growth metrics often have different data requirements.

 • In general, norm-referenced growth analyses tolerate assessment change
 whereas criterion-referenced growth analyses require.

REVIEW: THREATS TO CALCULATION

 • Growth metrics requiring a vertical scale for calculation will not be possible in
 the transition year without some type of scale equating.

 • Most growth analyses (e.g., SGPs, VAM) don’t require a vertical scale for
 calculation. Regardless of whether PARCC uses a vertical scale, SGPs can be
 calculated using both vertical and non-vertical scales.

 • A significant ceiling/floor associated with a test (either SBAC/PARCC or a state
 test used as a prior) can lead to bad model fit. These growth metrics often
 have different data requirements.

 • Barring significant ceiling/floor, norm-referenced analyses will very likely yield a
 uniform distribution of percentiles.

 • Changing achievement levels will require states using value-tables to redefine
 values 3 times in the coming years.

Wednesday, February 5, 14

REVIEW: REQUIREMENTS FOR CALCULATING
 GROWTH

 • Annual growth? Bi-annual growth? Tri-annual growth?

 • Annual growth requires (at a minimum) two consecutive annual measures (i.e.,
 scale scores) of student achievement (usually taken from the same content
 area).

 • Annual targets (Projections/Targets/Trajectories) require (at a minimum) two
 consecutive annual measures of student achievement from the same
 assessment (i.e., an assessment with a time-invariant scale) or scales that are
 equated such that they can be treated as equivalent.

Wednesday, February 5, 14

REVIEW: REQUIREMENTS FOR CALCULATING
 GROWTH
 • States primarily focus on annual growth, particularly for accountability
 (exceptions include, for example, student growth from 8th to 10th grade).

 • PARCC field testing will impact a state’s ability to calculate growth for students
 due to the simple fact that student will not receive back scale scores on the
 PARCC field test.

 • Absent double testing, students participating in the field test cannot receive
 annual student growth in BOTH 2013-2014 (no current year score) AND
 2014-2015 (no prior year score).

 • If a student has a scale score in 2012-2013, one could, for example, calculate a
 two year growth (e.g., a two year SGP) for a students participating in field
 testing between 2012-2013 and 2014-2015.

 • In the years after the transition, absent double testing, students will have
 different numbers of priors available for growth analyses.
Wednesday, February 5, 14

REVIEW: REQUIREMENTS FOR CALCULATING
 GROWTH: SUMMARY

 • Easier to conduct norm-referenced analyses during transition than criterion-
 referenced growth-to-standard analyses.

 • Criterion-referenced projections require linking analyses done exclusively on
 the PARCC/SBAC assessment in order to extrapolate forward how much
 growth is required to, for example catch-up/keep-up/move-up/stay-up.

 • Analogously growth-to-standard (e.g., career and college-readiness) will require
 at least two years data on the new scale as well as fixed achievement levels/
 standards defined on the new scale.

 • Establishing baseline referenced growth will likely require even more time (e.g.,
 4 years) to establish a stable baseline from which to compare going forward.

REQUIREMENTS FOR THE USE OF GROWTH
 • Two distinct challenges: Calculation and Use

 • Just because we can calculate student growth doesn’t mean it is defensible to
 use it for previously existing accountability purposes.

 • Validating growth use will require defining the purpose.

 • Current uses include:

 • Teacher and leader evaluation (required by RttT, ESEA waiver, state policy/rule making, ...)

 • School and District accountability (ESEA waiver, state policy, ...)

 • Charter school contracts.

 • Improvement planning

Wednesday, February 5, 14

REQUIREMENTS FOR THE USE OF GROWTH
 • During the assessment transition, a number of challenges confront states using
 growth for accountability purposes.

 • Data time span (e.g., two-year growth) not aligned with accountability time
 span (annual)

 • Changes in types of growth analyses done for accountability during
 transition. Without equating of state test to consortium test, projection/
 trajectory based criterion-referenced growth not available until year 2 of
 PARCC/SBAC.

 • Assessment results from different assessments (state and PARCC/SBAC).
 Depending upon the number of priors used by the state, this will be an
 ongoing issue for many years.

 • Missing data due to PARCC/SBAC field testing.

Wednesday, February 5, 14

REQUIREMENTS FOR THE USE OF GROWTH

 • Data time span (e.g., two-year growth) not aligned with accountability time
 span (annual)

 • Most accountability systems use an observational pre-post design to hold
 teachers/schools/districts accountable.

 • Often, the pre-test occurs the spring prior to enrollment in the unit of
 accountability and the post-test the spring during enrollment.

 • An extended growth time span (e.g., two-year) undermines the attribution
 of responsibility implicit within the accountability determination.
